Contour contours objects

Source: R/zz-gen-contour.R
go_contour_contours.Rd

The object for the contours of a contour trace (go_contour()). go_contour_contours() creates one, with exactly its properties; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_contour_contours(
  ...,
  coloring = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  labelfont = NULL,
  labelformat = NULL,
  operation = NULL,
  showlabels = NULL,
  showlines = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  value = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

...

Not for properties, which must be named in full: an abbreviated or unknown name is an error that suggests the right one.

coloring

Determines the coloring method showing the contour values. If "fill", coloring is done evenly between each contour level If "heatmap", a heatmap gradient coloring is applied between each contour level. If "lines", coloring is done on the contour lines. If "none", no coloring is applied on this trace. One of "fill", "heatmap", "lines", "none".

end

Sets the end contour level value. Must be more than `contours.start` Number.

labelfont

Sets the font used for labeling the contour levels. The default color comes from the lines, if shown. The default family and size come from `layout.font`. A go_font() object or named list, with properties color, family, lineposition, shadow, size, style, textcase, variant and weight (see go_font()).

labelformat

Sets the contour label formatting rule using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. String.

operation

Sets the constraint operation. "=" keeps regions equal to `value` "<" and "<=" keep regions less than `value` ">" and ">=" keep regions greater than `value` "[]", "()", "[)", and "(]" keep regions inside `value[0]` to `value[1]` "][", ")(", "](", ")[" keep regions outside `value[0]` to `value[1]` Open vs. closed intervals make no difference to constraint display, but all versions are allowed. One of "=", "<", ">=", ">", "<=", "[]", "()", "[)", "(]", "][", ")(", "](", ")[".

showlabels

Determines whether to label the contour lines with their values. Logical.

showlines

Determines whether or not the contour lines are drawn. Has an effect only if `contours.coloring` is set to "fill". Logical.

size

Sets the step between each contour level. Must be positive. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

start

Sets the starting contour level value. Must be less than `contours.end` Number.

type

If `levels`, the data is represented as a contour plot with multiple levels displayed. If `constraint`, the data is represented as constraints with the invalid region shaded as specified by the `operation` and `value` parameters. One of "levels", "constraint".

value

Sets the value or values of the constraint boundary. When `operation` is set to one of the comparison values (`=,<,>=,>,<=`) "value" is expected to be a number. When `operation` is set to one of the interval values (`[],(),[),(],][,)(,](,)[`) "value" is expected to be an array of two numbers where the first is the lower bound and the second is the upper bound. Any value.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_contour_contours object (a named list).

Details

Nested objects are named lists, or objects of the constructors their arguments name. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified. A property may be a one-sided formula (color = ~col): it is kept, and evaluated in the data (then checked) when its trace is added to a figure with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

Examples

airquality |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_contour(
    x = ~Day,
    y = ~Month,
    z = ~Temp,
    contours = go_contour_contours(size = 10)
  )
